title: Tidying Up the Conversational Recommender Systems’ Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review analyzing how recommender systems prioritize popular items, and exploring mitigation techniques for popularity and long-tail biases in conversational settings.
Systematic literature review of discrepancies between real-world interactions and recorded data, encompassing conformity, exposure, selection, and exploitation biases.
Systematic literature review examining the flaws in standard evaluation metrics and prioritizing evaluation of serendipity, diversity, and long-term fairness.
Systematic literature review assessing how systems inadvertently amplify societal biases based on sensitive user attributes such as gender, race, or age.
Systematic literature review evaluating users' tendency to interact with higher-ranked items regardless of actual relevance, and how language framing affects this.
Systematic literature review of the over-recommendation of similar content, leading to filter bubbles, preference amplification, and feedback loops.
Systematic literature review exploring how combinations of contextual biases (e.g., modality and popularity together) influence user decision-making.
Systematic literature review analyzing how previous recommendations and dialogue history disproportionately influence subsequent conversational recommendations.
Systematic literature review evaluating a system's tendency to focus on a narrow subset of assumed attributes that users prioritize when making decisions.
Systematic literature review examining how users alter their conversational behavior and speech patterns when knowing they are interacting with an AI bot.
Systematic literature review assessing multi-modal models' over-reliance on textual inputs while paying less attention to visual or non-textual signals.
Systematic literature review analyzing how user ambiguity or intentional manipulation limits system comprehension and recommendation quality.
Systematic literature review exploring human-like cognitive biases in language models, such as framing biases, uncertainty-aversion, and user trust bias.
Systematic literature review assessing unequal treatment or favoritism arising from societal stereotypes and historical data in language and recommendation algorithms.
Systematic literature review evaluating detrimental discrepancies, such as offensiveness or unequal treatment, when dialogue systems adopt different demographic personas.
